blocks.text: Born in Volhynia, he entered monastic life while young. He learned Scripture and icon painting and was ordained a priest-monk. He later led a community on the Rata River.

blocks.text: He became metropolitan through the Patriarchate of Constantinople. He traveled among clergy and people during Mongol domination, worked for peace among princes, and sought protection for the clergy. In 1325 he transferred his residence from Vladimir to Moscow.

blocks.text: Saint Peter died on December 21, 1326, and was buried in Moscow’s Dormition Cathedral. The life says he was numbered among the Saints in 1339. It describes repose rather than martyrdom.

blocks.text: His memory became closely associated with Moscow and its Dormition Cathedral, whose foundation he blessed in 1326. The source also remembers icons he painted. These roles distinguish him from the much later Metropolitan Saint Peter Mogila.

blocks.text: The OCA’s relics commemoration records three surviving letters. They concern priests’ pastoral responsibilities, conduct, and care for those entrusted to them, with an exhortation to laypeople to keep Christ’s commandments.
